## Synopsis

Open every signing key that strazad opens at start with the key-encryption
key strazad runs with, secret.key, and seal it with the key in --new-kek-file,
then exit without serving. Each key goes from one seal to the other in a
single write. A retired session or client assertion key stays as it is.

Run it when you replace secret.key. Stop every strazad replica first, write
32 random bytes to the new file, run this command, put the new file in place
of secret.key on every replica, and start strazad. Stored credentials stay
sealed under the old key, so set each one again after the start.

Give the command the same --config, --profile, --data-dir and --store-dsn
that strazad serve runs with, so that it finds the same database and key.

```
strazad reseal-signing-keys --new-kek-file <path> [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --config string         config file path (default: $STRAZA_CONFIG, else ./straza.yaml when it exists)
      --data-dir string       local state directory (default data)
      --new-kek-file string   the file that holds the new 32-byte key-encryption key
      --profile string        governance profile, standalone or enterprise (default standalone); it decides every other default
      --store-dsn string      store DSN: a SQLite file path or a PostgreSQL connection string (default: <data-dir>/straza.db on SQLite; PostgreSQL needs one here, in store.dsn or in STRAZA_STORE_DSN)
```
